title: On‑Prem Image Trust and Canary Release Workflow (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic operational playbook for on-prem/VPC private deployments focusing on two operational goals: (1) ensure image provenance and cryptographic trust for images we deploy into customer environments, and (2) standardize a safe canary and rollback flow implemented via GitOps (ArgoCD) + Helm with Terraform-managed infra.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Private (VPC / on-prem) manifests and artifacts that customers will run in their clusters.
- We assume images are built in CI in our build cluster and pushed to customer-allowed registries (or pulled via mirror proxies).
- Customers may require signed images (cosign/notation) + attestation (SLSA/Link).
- Terraform manages infra (VPC routing, image mirror proxies, KMS), Helm manages app release, ArgoCD performs GitOps reconciliation.
- This is operator-facing; includes runbook steps for engineers and SREs.

High-level workflow summary:
1) Build -> sign -> attest -> push
   - Build in CI (GitHub Actions/Gitlab CI).
   - Create digest-based tag (sha256) and sign with Cosign using a team KMS key (or customer-provided KMS).
   - Produce SLSA-style provenance attestation and store in registry or artifact bucket.
2) Publish and mirror
   - Push to canonical registry (e.g., private ECR/Harbor). If customer uses pull-through mirror, push to mirror endpoint and update mirror config via Terraform.
3) Create GitOps release bundle
   - Update the Helm values in the release repo (image.digest, image.signatureRef, chart version). Open PR to repo that ArgoCD watches.
4) Canary rollout via ArgoCD + Helm
   - Use Helm chart with canary-enabled values. ArgoCD app defines progressive rollout ("blue/green" or "canary": replica skew + service routing).
5) Monitor health and commit or rollback
   - Evaluate smoke tests, perf metrics, and error budget. If thresholds breached -> automatic rollback (ArgoCD rollback + Helm rollback).

Concrete CI snippets (example):
- Build step (pseudo):
  - docker build -t registry.example.com/redwood/service:sha-$(GIT_SHA) .
  - docker push registry.example.com/redwood/service:sha-$(GIT_SHA)
- Sign (cosign + KMS):
  - COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=true cosign sign --key k8s://projects/myproj/locations/global/keyRings/foo/cryptoKeys/cosign-key registry.example.com/redwood/service@sha256:<digest>
- Attest (slsa provenance):
  - in-toto/slsa-generator > provenance.json
  - cosign attach --signature provenance.json registry...

Helm values conventions (recommend):
- image:
  - repository: registry.example.com/redwood/service
  - digest: sha256:xxxxx  # canonical immutable ref
  - signed: true
  - signatureRef: cosign:sha256:xxxxx # reference used by admission/
- rollout:
  - strategy: Canary
  - canary:
    - steps: [10,30,100]           # percentages or traffic split steps
    - pauseSeconds: 300           # smoke window

ArgoCD integration patterns:
- App per-environment: each customer cluster has an Argo App pointing at a dedicated env repo branch.
- App health checks use custom Lua or k8s probes to check readiness, smoke endpoints, and custom metrics (latency p50/p95).
- Use AppProject to restrict which clusters and namespaces an app can target.
- Automate PR -> ArgoCD sync flow with status checks in CI; require signed commit (CI adds signature file).

Admission and enforcement options (in-cluster):
- Admission webhook (optional) that verifies image signatures and SLSA attestations before allowing pull. Use cosign verification + policy engine (OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno).
- If cluster uses image mirror proxy, enforce image digest pinning and signature verification at the pull-through proxy.

Terraform module notes (high-level):
- Module: private-deploy/registry-mirror
  - inputs: mirror_endpoint, allowed_cidrs, kms_key_id, signing_key_location
  - outputs: mirror_url, secret_arn
  - state: remote state in customer S3/GCS bucket + state locking (DynamoDB or GCS locks).
- Module: private-deploy/argocd-bootstrap
  - creates ArgoCD instance (helm_release), service account, and Project constraints.
  - ensures RBAC minimal rights, network policies and TLS certs via cert-manager.
- Module: private-deploy/kms-roles
  - maps team/service IAM principals to a KMS key; policy allows only CI issuer to sign images.
- Notes on immutability and drift:
  - Avoid storing mutable tags in TF state. Always prefer digest refs or compute digest in CI and pass as variable via TF var or Git commit.
  - Use lifecycle rules: prevent_destroy=false only for ephemeral infra.

Upgrade plan and canary timeline (example for a minor release):
- T-72h: Build, sign, smoke-run image in canary cluster (internal).
- T-48h: Produce attestation, open env PR with canary image.digest, run CI (automated tests + policy checks).
- T-24h: Merge to staging branch, ArgoCD starts canary sync (10% traffic).
- T+30m: Run smoke-suite (synthetic traffic, core use-cases).
- T+3h: If all green, proceed to 30% step, then 100% after 12h observation.
- Rollback window: first 6 hours after merge are critical; if error budget breached, rollback automatically.

Rollback and remediation playbook (on-call):
- Triggering conditions (any of): error rate > 2x baseline, latency p95 > baseline + 200ms, failed smoke tests, data loss indicators.
- Immediate steps:
  - Open incident Slack channel and tag #private-deploy-oncall.
  - Identify ArgoCD Application and run: argocd app rollback <app> --revision <previous-good-revision> OR helm rollback <release> 1
  - Revoke routing changes in service mesh (Envoy/Contour) to shift traffic back.
  - If cause is bad image signature or missing attestation: block new PRs via branch protection and add a policy failure ticket.
- Post-incident: collect artifacts (ci logs, cosign verification outputs, provenance.json, ArgoCD events), write RCA, update policy gaps.

Security & key management checklist:
- KMS keys used for signing must be rotated annually; rotation policy documented in terraform module.
- Use customer-managed keys when requested; provide proof-of-possession flow to map signing key to CI principal.
- Limit cosign private key access to build CI ephemeral runners or to a secure signing service (no long-lived keys on developer machines).

Verification and smoke tests (automated):
- verify-image-signature.sh <image>
  - cosign verify --key k8s://... <image> || exit 2
  - check provenance existence (curl registry/.../attestations)
- smoke-suite: small end-to-end script that runs representative prompts/embeddings, asserts outputs for regressions, and records latencies.

Operational hardening notes (lessons learned):
- Don’t rely on mutable tags in GitOps; stick to digests.
- Keep canary windows small but meaningful; long windows delay rollout, short ones risk missing regressions. Aim for progressive steps 10/30/100 with automated checks at each step.
- Maintain a small set of verified test prompts and golden traces per customer for targeted regression checks (store in vault/secure bucket).
- For air-gapped customers, include a signed bundle option (tarball of images + Helm charts + attestations) and a verified import script that will assert signatures locally.

Open TODOs / action items:
- [ ] Define mandatory attestation fields (builder, buildType, sourceCommit, invocationId).
- [ ] Create a templated GitHub Action that outputs cosign signature + provenance and posts digest to a release channel. (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Prototype an OPA policy that verifies cosign signatures and enforces a minimum SLSA level (owner: Sofia).
- [ ] Update terraform module docs with example usage for customer KMS integration (owner: Marco).

References / useful commands:
- cosign docs: https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/
- SLSA provenance examples: https://slsa.dev/provenance/
- ArgoCD progressive sync docs and AppProject examples (see linked artifacts).
- Example verify script: ./deploy/scripts/verify-image-and-attestation.sh

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc light; separate checklist into a customer-runbook + internal operator playbook.
- Follow-up meeting with solutions-engineering to align on customer onboarding checklist and required artifacts for air-gapped deployments.

End.
